transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

I... well, my boss told me I had to come. They got scared at work. I guess I was just... I don't know, freezing up while I was supposed to be waiting tables. Or I'd be doing things wrong. Like, I was standing over by the soda station with the key to the cash drawer... and I was just saying table numbers over and over instead of actually closing out the checks. I didn't mean to.

During that time when you were freezing up and repeating the table numbers, did you feel disconnected from your body or surroundings, like things weren't real, or like you were watching yourself from outside?
No... I don't think so. It wasn't like I was watching myself from the outside or anything. I was just... there. Just stuck, I guess.
When did this freezing up and difficulty concentrating at work first start happening? Was it sudden, or did it come on gradually over days or weeks?

I don't know... it wasn't sudden. It's been happening for a while now. Maybe... a year and a couple of months? Ever since they asked me to be the shift lead for the evenings. Things just started getting harder after that.
Over this past year or so, when you're not at work, how has your mood been? Do you find yourself feeling down, sad, or hopeless most of the time, or are you more worried and nervous about things?
I don't know... I wouldn't really say I'm sad. Or nervous. I just... I don't know. I just go home. It's fine, I guess.
Over this past year, have you noticed any physical symptoms that bother you? Things like headaches, muscle tension, tiredness, or stomach problems?
No... I don't think so. I haven't really noticed anything like that. I feel fine physically, I guess.
When you think about work or your responsibilities, do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when things are going okay?
I don't think so. Um... I don't really think about it when I'm not there. It's just work.
Over this past year or so, have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy doing, or does nothing feel as fun or satisfying as it used to?

I guess... I don't really do much anymore. I used to like walking on the beach, baking, gardening... writing in my journal. But I just don't. And when my husband tries to talk to me, I just sit there. I don't know. It's like I just can't get myself to care about starting anything.
Over this past year, have you noticed changes in your sleep—like sleeping more than usual, sleeping less, or having trouble falling asleep?
Um... no. I sleep fine, I think. Just... normal. I haven't noticed any changes.
Over this past year or so, would you say that most days you've been feeling empty or down, even on days when nothing particular is wrong?
Um... no. I don't really feel sad or anything. I just... I don't know. I don't think so.

When you think about doing those things you used to enjoy—like walking on the beach or baking—do you want to do them but just can't seem to get started, or is it that you don't really want to do them anymore because they wouldn't feel enjoyable?
I don't know... I just... I don't really want to do them. It just doesn't seem like it would matter.
When you think about your life right now, do you feel like things are hopeless or that nothing will get better, or do you feel like things could improve?
I don't really think about it... I just... I don't know. It's just how it is.
Over this past year, have you felt like you're worthless or that things are your fault, even when logically you know that might not be true?
No... not really. I don't think about it like that. I just... I don't know.

When you're doing everyday activities like eating or spending time with your husband, do you actually feel pleasure or enjoyment from those things, or does everything just feel kind of flat and empty?

I don't know... it's mostly just flat, I guess. Like... when my husband tries to talk with me, I mostly just sit there. I just... it feels like I can't get myself to care. Or start anything. I don't really go for beach walks or bake much anymore. Or garden... or write in my journal. I just... don't.
